o: Includes an additional anti-rotation pin or screw in the neck

en.q: For an open femoral shaft fracture Gustilo IIIB, the appropriate strategy is:
o: Debridement, temporary external fixation, then delayed nailing after soft-tissue coverage
Primary external fixation as definitive treatment

en.q: The Winquist-Hansen classification grades:
Which structures are at risk with medial-to-lateral distal locking screws?
o: Saphenous nerve and femoral artery in adductor canal

en.q: Retrograde IM nail entry point is:
o: Just anterior to PCL insertion in intercondylar notch

en.q: Which nerve is at risk in segmental/distal femoral fracture?
Common issue in very distal third with antegrade nailing:
Why does subtrochanteric proximal fragment go flexion-abduction-ER?
o: M. iliopsoas (flex), gluteus medius/minimus (abd), short external rotators

en.q: AO 32-C is:
Most common neurologic deficit after femoral nailing on a fracture table:
o: Pudendal nerve injury from perineal post

en.q: Which neurovascular structures are at risk in lateral femoral approach?
o: Sciatic nerve and its branches (especially with retrograde low approaches) and femoral nerve in Hunter's canal manipulations

en.q: With distal shaft fracture near popliteal level, most important is:
o: Assessment of pulses (popliteal artery), ABI, possibly CT angiography

en.q: Most likely complication of retrograde femoral nailing in a young patient:
o: Knee articular cartilage injury, infection risk, heterotopic ossification

en.q: The Winquist-Hansen classification describes:
Greater trochanter tip entry carries the risk of:
Pudendal nerve injury during traction-table positioning may result from:
o: Pressure from the perineal post during traction

en.q: Retrograde nailing is favoured in:
o: Pregnant patient with distal femoral fracture

en.q: Threshold for thigh fasciotomy:
The femoral shaft extends from approximately 5 cm distal to the lesser trochanter to:
o: 6 cm proximal to the adductor tubercle

en.q: Reamer-Irrigator-Aspirator (RIA):
o: Is a drainage system for infected canal
Reduces intramedullary pressure during reaming in polytrauma

en.q: Conversion from external fixation to IM nail is recommended within:
o: 5–14 days before pin tract infection risk rises

en.q: Patient positioning for antegrade nailing may be:
o: Supine on fracture table or lateral decubitus on regular table

en.q: Retrograde nailing is particularly indicated in:
o: Bilateral femoral shaft fractures or ipsilateral acetabular fracture

en.q: Standard nonunion management after IM nailing is:
Rotational profile assessment of the femur is best by:
o: CT rotational profile vs contralateral side

en.q: Antibiotic management of higher-grade open femoral fractures typically includes:
o: Cefazolin plus aminoglycoside in higher grades
